notes.text: Implied ERP 4.23% at the start of 2026, 4.37% at the start of March and 4.51% by March 13 (index fell Feb 27-Mar 13 while oil rose above $100). notes.title: AI's Winners, Losers and Wannabes: An NVIDIA Valuation, with the AI Boost!
notes.text: Values it at about $240 a share as of June 10, 2023 when it traded at $409 (it rose to $434 by June 20): overvalued. Base case: revenue $267 billion in 2033 with AI chip revenue growing about tenfold, a 15% share of auto chips and 15% annual growth in gaming and other; R&D-adjusted operating margin 35% next year rising to 40% by 2027 (range 30-50%); sales-to-capital 1.15 vs 0.65 historically; cost of capital starting at 12.21% and drifting to 8.85%. A value above $400 is possible but unlikely; the price is "pushing towards the 95th percentile" and breakeven needs extraordinary growth plus margins near 50%. Bought in 2018 after a drop of over 50% and sold half at these prices, keeping the rest for optionality. Flags dependence on TSMC and China-Taiwan risk.

notes.text: Values enterprise value at $1.22 trillion and equity at $1.3 trillion, about $100 a share (the equity rises mostly from $75 billion of IPO cash). 2025 revenue grew about one-third (connectivity almost 50%, AI about 22%, space 7.64%); 2025 operating loss $2.57 billion, net loss about $5 billion. Cost of capital 8.37% at the start and 8.25% in steady state. Book equity $41.3 billion, debt including leases $22.9 billion, cash $24.7 billion, 12,535 million shares. Calls the reported $28 trillion total addressable market "fantasy." An offering price near $135 a share (about $1.8 trillion) is "too richly priced" against his $1.25-$1.35 trillion range: overvalued at the rumored price. notes.text: Base-case intrinsic value $1.22 trillion; simulation median $1.29 trillion across 10,000 runs (no per-share value; cash and debt ignored). Not a buy at the rumored $1.75 trillion IPO price: "one big correction away from being fairly priced or even cheap," and he would then buy. 2025 revenue about $15.6 billion (launch about $4.1 billion, Starlink and related about $11.4 billion, xAI subscriptions about $100 million); estimated EBITDA $8 billion; cost of capital 8%. Musk owns about 42% of equity and about 80% of the votes. At $1.25 trillion EV: about 80x sales and 156x EBITDA. Segment assumptions: launch market $30 billion growing to $100 billion by 2036, share falling from over 80% to 70%, margin 40%; Starlink internet market $15 billion to $160 billion, share 75%, margin near 60% (about 10,000 satellites and over 10 million subscribers at end-2025); xAI 2036 revenue $80 billion at a 50% margin; expansion options $50 billion of revenue at a 30% margin after 2032. Calls the 8% cost of capital reasonable because the risk is company-specific and two-sided.
